extracted.intended_audience: academic economists, innovation scholars, and empirical researchers studying corporate R&D, patent-publication links, and knowledge spillovers
extracted.subtask_short: measuring firm use of scientific publications
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical specification and measurement strategies for linking firms' scientific publications to patenting activity and firm outcomes (publications, R&D productivity, market value). Covers construction of internal/external citation measures, heterogeneity, IV identification, and sample/matching procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal patent citation measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal citation: a patent citation made by a firm's own patents to its own scientific publications (patent citations to science).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the primary measure of 'use of science in invention'. Empirically associated with future publications (one additional internal citation associated with ~0.5 additional publications per firm-year in firm FE specification). Alternative measures of internal citation were used in robustness checks (Columns 6-8) and all yield a positive relationship with publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Between- vs within-firm specification (firm fixed effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimating both cross-sectional (between-firm averages) and within-firm (firm fixed effects) relationships to distinguish heterogeneity across firms from within-firm changes over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Column 1 (pooled) showed a large coefficient (0.68) that fell sharply to 0.11 in firm-FE estimates, indicating much of the raw correlation is driven by across-firm heterogeneity; firm-FE estimates remain statistically significant but smaller. Use firm fixed effects to control for time-invariant firm heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness checks for citation measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform robustness analyses: restrict sample to firms with at least one publication; control for self-citations (internal patent citations to own patents); exclude examiner-added citations; exclude inventor self-citations; lag RHS variables by 2-3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columns 4-8 present these checks. Controlling for self-citations leaves main coefficient stable while self-citation coefficient is statistically zero. Excluding examiner citations and inventor self-citations leaves results robust. Lagging RHS variables preserves positive/significant internal citation effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recency of cited science (new vs old science)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish citations to recent science (publications no older than five years from the grant year of the citing patent) versus citations to older science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal citations to recent science have positive and significant effects on future publications (e.g., 0.130), while citations to old science have no effect—implies recentness matters for signaling/use in downstream R&D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic vs applied classification of cited publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify cited journals/publications as basic or applied using CHI index categories or Journal Impact Factor (JIF): basic = top CHI categories / above-median JIF; applied otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximately 70% of internal citations are to basic science journals and these citations drive the production of future publications. Internal citations to basic science are positive and statistically significant; applied-science citations are not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication quality (high vs low) based on normalized citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify publications into high- and low-quality using the number of citations an article receives divided by the average citations for all WoS publications in the same journal-year; split at the median within the corporate publications sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only citations to high-quality publications matter for inducing future publications (high-quality internal citation coefficient positive/significant; low-quality citations statistically zero).

rubrics_metrics.name: Core vs non-core technology of citing patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a firm's core technology as the IPC class containing the majority of the firm's patents in a given year; classify citations from patents in core vs non-core areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core citations (citations by patents in the firm's core technology) have a stronger relationship with future publications. Moving from core to non-core citing patents reduces the internal citation coefficient (e.g., from 0.12 to 0.04). About 40% of internal citations are by core patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing patent quality (high vs low)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure patent quality as number of citations a patent receives divided by average citations for patents granted in the same year; classify high/low by median within corporate patents sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal citation—publication relationship is stronger for high-quality citing patents, though coefficients on high and low quality patents are not always statistically different (e.g., 0.091 vs 0.054).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrumental variable: inventor-author overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct inventor-author overlap at firm-year level as the share of patents with inventors who are also authors of a firm publication published no later than three years from the focal patent’s grant year (defined only for publishing firms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a first-stage determinant of internal citation: higher overlap increases probability of internal citation. Within-firm estimates show a one-standard-deviation increase in overlap raises the probability of internal citation by ~30% relative to sample mean. Check that overlap does not predict external citations to mitigate concerns about general propensity to cite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrumental variable: Inevitable Disclosure Doctrine (IDD) × mobility risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct an instrument IDD_mobility = IDD_state × mobility_risk, where IDD_state is a dummy if the state's courts apply IDD in year t, and mobility_risk is the number of rival publishing firms in the same 4-digit SIC within 100 miles of the focal firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification assumption: adoption of IDD affects inventor-author overlap (and hence internal citations) but not directly firms' incentives to invest in research. Test for exogeneity by checking no correlation between changes in IDD and technological opportunities (patents per R&D, publications per R&D). First-stage shows strong instrument (Kleibergen-Paap F = 72).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative instrument: profit shocks from currency devaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use industry-level profit shocks due to foreign exchange devaluation that affect dependence of inventions on science as an alternative source of exogenous variation in internal citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Devaluation associated with drops in profits and fewer internal citations—consistent with decreased exploratory science in lean times. Combined IV using IDD and devaluation passes overidentification tests (Hansen) in appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge spillovers: external citation measures
rubrics_metrics.description: External citations are citations to a firm's publications made by other firms' patents (outsider citations); build measures of external use weighted by product-market proximity (SEGMENT) and technology proximity (TECH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory predicts profit-reducing spillovers when rivals (close in product market) use the knowledge. Empirically, external citation coefficient is negative and statistically indistinguishable from zero overall; SEGMENT-weighted external citations are negatively related to publications when restricting to recent publications and publishing firms, while TECH-weighted citations can be positively related.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEGMENT and TECH proximity construction
rubrics_metrics.description: SEGMENT: absolute un-centered correlation between firms' sales segment share vectors (4-digit SIC); TECH: cosine similarity between patent-share vectors across 4-digit IPC classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute SEGMENT- and TECH-weighted external citation counts by weighting outsider citations by proximity. Use Compustat operating segments for sales shares and patent distributions for TECH. Expect SEGMENT-weighted citations to capture profit-reducing spillovers; no clear prediction for TECH.

rubrics_metrics.name: R&D productivity measure (citation-weighted patents per R&D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation-weighted patents: annual flow of patents weighted by the ratio of citations each patent receives to the average number of citations received by all patents granted in the same year; dependent variable ln(1 + Citation weighted patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regression includes Share of Inter citation (ratio of internal citations from own patents to citations received from all corporate patents), lagged R&D stock, publication stock, firm fixed effects. Expect firms with higher share of internal citation to show higher R&D productivity. Interaction with R&D stock positive and significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of internal citation (Share of Inter citation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of Inter citation = internal citations from own patents divided by number of citations received from all corporate patents; average value 0.013, SD 0.093.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a key explanatory variable in R&D productivity regressions; interacts positively with R&D stock to predict citation-weighted patent output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications stock weighted by internal/external citations (Internal pub stock / External pub stock)
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal pub stockt = Internal pubt + Internal pub stockt-1, where Internal pubt is the number of internal citations publications receive in year t; External pub stock is computed analogously using external citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in market-value regressions as ln(1 + Internal pub stock) and ln(1 + External pub stock). Interpret coefficients as 'shadow prices' or imputed value attributable to the asset (publications stock). Decompose external stock into SEGMENT- and TECH-weighted components to separate rival vs technical spillovers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market value regression specification
rubrics_metrics.description: ln(Market valueit) regressed on ln(1 + Internal pub stockit-1), ln(1 + External pub stockit-1), ln Assetsit-1, and controls Z (lagged sales, R&D stock, patents stock), with firm and year fixed effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect internal pub stock coefficient positive and external pub stock coefficient negative (due to rival spillovers). Empirically, internal coefficient positive; aggregate external coefficient can be positive but SEGMENT-weighted external citations are negative (as theoretically expected), while TECH-weighted may be positive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent quality normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent quality = number of citations a patent receives divided by average citations received by all patents granted in the same year; classify patents into high/low quality by median value in the corporate patents sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to examine heterogeneity: internal citation—publication relationship stronger for citations made by high-quality patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample construction and firm identifier procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct an unbalanced panel of publicly traded US-headquartered firms (1980–2006) with at least one year of positive R&D expenditures and at least one patent; final sample: 4,736 firms and 57,765 firm-year observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address parent-subsidiary identifier issues by (i) using NBER 2006 patent data to identify multiple Compustat records per company, (ii) merging parent and subsidiary records using CGS Associated Issuers database and manual modifications, (iii) assign a unique 9-digit CUSIP (UO-COMPANY) and NBER PDPCO code and up to five associated CUSIPs. Exclude non-patenting and non-US-headquartered firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching publications to firms (Web of Science selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Match firm sample to publications from Web of Science, including articles from 'Science Citation Index' and 'Conference Proceedings Citation Index - Science', excluding social sciences, arts and humanities articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures include matching scientific publications to Compustat companies, mapping patent citations to publications, matching patent data to Compustat, and dynamic matching of Compustat accounting information. Appendix provides detailed matching algorithms and examples (e.g., handling multiple affiliations strings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Control variables and fixed effects in regressions
rubrics_metrics.description: All specifications control for firm fixed effects (and sometimes industry dummies), R&D stock, patent stock, sales, assets, state employment, and year fixed effects as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control set and fixed effects used to mitigate confounding factors (time-invariant firm heterogeneity, state-level time-varying factors). For IV estimations, include state employment to mitigate unobserved state heterogeneity.
